items.title: Anthropic Closes Record $30B Funding Round — Valued at $380B
items.summary: Anthropic closed a record-setting $30 billion funding round, now valued at $380 billion. The round was led by Coatue and GIC. Anthropic also aired two commercials during Super Bowl LX as part of a broader marketing campaign. Separately, Anthropic expanded Claude's free tier to include file creation, third-party connectors (Slack, Notion, Zapier, Figma), and skills — countering OpenAI's move to show ads on ChatGPT's free tier.
items.relevance: Massive validation for the platform you're building on. $30B in funding means Anthropic has a long runway — Claude isn't going anywhere. The expanded free tier with connectors could be useful for AVA's community outreach or T1D family support tools. Anthropic is clearly winning the 'developer trust' war vs OpenAI's ad-supported model.

items.title: US Military Used Claude in Venezuela Raid via Palantir — Raises Policy Questions
items.summary: Anthropic's Claude was used in the U.S. military operation that captured former Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro, deployed through Palantir's classified platforms. This marks a significant milestone for AI in military operations. Anthropic's usage policies technically forbid using Claude to support violence or surveillance, creating tension with this deployment. The Pentagon is pushing AI companies to expand access on classified networks.
items.relevance: This is a landmark moment for AI — Claude being used in an actual military operation is unprecedented. It raises real questions about AI ethics and usage policies. Worth watching how Anthropic responds, since their stated policies conflict with military use. For you as a builder on Claude: the technology is clearly capable of high-stakes real-world operations, which is both impressive and sobering.

items.title: ByteDance's Seedance 2.0 Goes Viral — AI Video Generation Gets Cinematic
items.summary: ByteDance launched Seedance 2.0, an AI video model capable of generating cinematic-quality videos from text prompts. It processes text, images, audio, and video simultaneously. Elon Musk commented 'It's happening fast' on X. The model is being compared to DeepSeek's disruption of the text AI space — this time for video. Designed for professional film, e-commerce, and advertising production.
items.relevance: AI video generation hitting cinematic quality has big implications for indie creators. For AVA marketing: you could potentially create promotional videos for the app or diabetes education content using AI video tools instead of hiring production teams. Keep an eye on when Seedance 2.0 becomes accessible outside China — could be a game-changer for marketing on a budget.

items.title: ADA 2026 Standards of Care — Major Updates for CGM, AID Systems, and School/Workplace Access
items.summary: The American Diabetes Association published 2026 Standards of Care with significant updates: AID systems no longer require minimum C-peptide levels or islet autoantibodies for T1D initiation, expanding access. New guidance facilitates CGM and insulin delivery system use in schools and workplaces, ensuring kids and adults get proper time to monitor glucose. Emphasis on selecting glucose-lowering therapies across clinical contexts.
items.relevance: Directly impacts both Kam and Kaislyn. Removing barriers to AID initiation means more kids get pumps sooner. The school/workplace guidance is huge — Kaislyn's school should now have clearer ADA-backed guidelines for supporting her CGM and pump use. For AVA: these expanded access guidelines mean a larger potential user base for the simulation app, as more newly-diagnosed kids get tech earlier.

items.title: Claude Code v2.1.41-42 — Agent Teams Fix, Auth CLI, Windows ARM64, Performance Boosts
items.summary: Recent Claude Code releases (v2.1.39-2.1.42) bring several improvements: guard against launching Claude Code inside another session, fixed Agent Teams model identifiers for Bedrock/Vertex, new CLI auth commands (login/status/logout), Windows ARM64 support, improved startup performance by deferring schema construction, better prompt cache hit rates, and multiple stability fixes for streaming and session handling.
items.relevance: The improved prompt cache hit rates directly reduce your API costs — fewer cache misses means cheaper Claude Code sessions. The auth CLI commands make it easier to manage multiple accounts or switch contexts. Agent Teams fixes matter if you scale Clawdbot to use multi-agent collaboration. Keep your Claude Code updated.

items.title: Xcode 26.3 Adds Agentic Coding — Claude and Codex Now Built Into Apple's IDE
items.summary: Apple released Xcode 26.3 with native integration of Anthropic's Claude Agent and OpenAI's Codex directly in the IDE. Developers can now automate repetitive tasks, generate intelligent code snippets, and troubleshoot within Xcode's workflow. This represents a shift toward agentic AI systems in development environments, where AI acts autonomously to assist with coding tasks.
items.relevance: This is directly relevant to AVA development. Claude Agent built into Xcode means you can get AI-assisted SwiftUI coding without leaving the IDE. For the ~80% complete AVA Type 1 app, this could accelerate the final push — especially for complex simulation logic and UI polish. Worth updating Xcode if you haven't already.

items.title: Tandem Diabetes Q4 Earnings Feb 19 — Analysts See 38% Upside, Revenue Growth Accelerating
items.summary: Tandem Diabetes Care reports Q4 2025 earnings on February 19. Analysts expect $277M revenue (up from $249M Q3), near-breakeven EPS. Stifel Nicolaus raised its price target, citing strong adoption trends for the t:slim X2 and AID systems. The company's stock has 38.4% potential upside according to consensus. Healthy financials signal continued R&D investment in the platform.
items.relevance: Kaislyn's pump company reporting strong numbers. Watch the Feb 19 call for announcements about next-gen features, Dexcom G8 compatibility, or Mobi pump expansion. Strong Tandem financials = continued innovation on the platform Kaislyn depends on. If they announce new kid-friendly features, that could inform AVA's companion device design too.

items.title: OpenAI Launches Codex-Spark on Cerebras Hardware — Ultra-Low-Latency Coding AI
items.summary: OpenAI partnered with Cerebras to launch Codex-Spark, running on Cerebras' Wafer Scale Engine 3 for ultra-low-latency AI coding inference. This gives Codex a 'latency-first' serving tier designed for new interaction patterns and real-time coding experiences. The partnership signals a trend toward specialized hardware for different AI workloads, moving beyond Nvidia's dominance.
items.relevance: Competition for Claude Code's coding market. OpenAI investing in custom hardware for coding AI suggests they see real-time code assistance as a key battleground. For you: more competition means better tools and lower prices over time. Worth trying Codex-Spark to compare with Claude Code for specific SwiftUI tasks, but Claude's Xcode integration likely gives it the edge for your workflow.
